pair.title: Pair with {name}
pair.description:
Home Assistant will register itself with the projector as a controller, the same way the smartphone app does.

1. Make sure the projector is switched on (projecting or in standby) and within range of a Bluetooth adapter or ESPHome Bluetooth proxy.
2. In the smartphone app, check that **Settings → Network → Restrict adding smartphones** is off.
3. Submit to pair. Home Assistant will appear as "Home Assistant" under **Smartphones added**. Pairing can take up to a minute.

reauth_confirm.title: Pair {name} again
reauth_confirm.description:
The projector rejected Home Assistant on more than one connection in a row. Usually "Home Assistant" was removed from **Smartphones added** or the projector was reset, and pairing again fixes it: make sure the projector is on and **Restrict adding smartphones** is off, then submit.

If "Home Assistant" is still in **Smartphones added** but set to **Deny**, set it to **Allow** in the app first. With more than one Bluetooth adapter or proxy, the pairing belongs to the one that made it; pairing through another adds a second "Home Assistant" entry.

On submit, Home Assistant first checks whether the projector accepts it again, and pairs only if it does not.

confirm.description: Every request to the projector times out, usually because its internal link is stuck. Home Assistant can try to restart it first, as the **Restart** button does, and then wait up to about two minutes for it to respond. The button below starts the attempt. Whether Restart gets through in this state has not been tried yet. If it does not help, or to fix it right away, press the recessed **RESET** button next to the DC IN jack; settings and pairings survive. This issue goes away once the projector responds again.

progress.restart: Trying Restart; waiting up to about two minutes for {name} to respond. Rather not wait? Close this window and press the recessed **RESET** button next to the DC IN jack.

abort.restart_not_answered: {name} did not answer Restart either and still does not respond two minutes later. Press the recessed **RESET** button next to the DC IN jack; settings and pairings survive.
abort.restart_did_not_help: Restart was sent, but {name} still does not respond two minutes later. Press the recessed **RESET** button next to the DC IN jack; settings and pairings survive.
abort.not_reached: Home Assistant could not reach {name} just now ({error}). It may be switched off or out of range, which Restart cannot help with. Try again once it is back; if every request then still times out, press the recessed **RESET** button next to the DC IN jack.
abort.not_loaded: The integration is not running for this projector right now. Reload it and try again.
abort.attempt_timed_out: Trying Restart took too long, and {name} still does not respond. Press the recessed **RESET** button next to the DC IN jack; settings and pairings survive.
abort.startup_did_not_help: {name} was starting up already and still does not respond two minutes later. Press the recessed **RESET** button next to the DC IN jack; settings and pairings survive.

init.description: Show the weather from Home Assistant on the projector's Weather poster.

data_description.weather_entity: Sent to the projector while its Weather poster is shown: when the poster appears and when the condition changes. When the picture has to change, the projector briefly shows another poster to draw it. Leave empty to leave the poster alone.
